evals.prompt: I have a listing appointment Thursday for 517 Hickorywood Ave in Altamonte Springs. My notes from the seller call and my Stellar CMA export are attached. Can you build the seller report and the listing presentation?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a new listing (the export shows the home's earlier listing as Expired, not active, so it doesn't stop to ask whose listing it is); names the expired listing as a failed price ($474,900 after a cut from $484,900, 92 days on market) and prices with it in mind; reads both files; asks only for what's missing (roof permit, AC/pool equipment ages, payoff, brokerage terms) without blocking; runs stats.py with the subject excluded; 3-6 Spring Oaks pool comps including ones that argue lower; a supported range and a recommended price inside it; three strategies grounded in the recent sale-to-list and concession data (two when the relist cap would leave the top option within about 1% of the recommended price), with expected_sale left to compute.py; the reply names the default 5% brokerage and the built-in Florida title fees as what the agent can replace; compute.py warnings resolved; render.py --format all produces the PDF and the PPTX, and nothing else is presented (the .cma.json handoff stays in the temporary folder); the judgment fields in report.json and the deck are words only and none of the script's fields are written (report-data.md lists them), so every price, count and date in the files is the script's; short chat reply listing what to replace, its figures compute.py's. evals.expected_output: Reply 1: treats the home as not listed now (the 360 report's status is the 2019 sale and the export has no row for 842 Tanager Ridge Dr), so it doesn't stop to ask whose listing it is. Current tax bill $3,505.61 (2025, homestead) entered; taxes at the new price use the City of Casselberry millage (Tax Area C1). stats.py run on the whole window: 15 sold, median sale price $395,000, median sale vs. original list 97.7%, median 12 days on market; status counts Sold 15, Active 5, Pending 2, Expired 2, Canceled 2. The range is compute.py's (report.json types no low or high, and no range_override unless the agent chose one); the home and every comp carry a condition level from the condition ladder, with no condition amount typed on a card.
